what: A spend-cap contract said the cap held before each paid call, and the work that followed it checked the cap once per case using a one-call worst case, while a single case could make several paid calls in a row — a gap every worker's own regression tests missed, caught only at review.
rule: A spend-cap or limit contract must name the exact unit that is checked (each paid call, not each case/task) and require one test where a single case makes several such calls, tripping the cap mid-way through that one case rather than only across accumulated cases.
fix: Enforcement: the shared contract template's own test-plan section now asks for exactly that. Template change only; no code check.
